_readme: THE LANE CONTRACT (DRE-2726). One file, read by everything.
Per lane: the entrance condition, the exit condition, the permitted writers,
and the evidence that justifies occupancy. The guard (scripts/lane_scope.py)
reads its flow from here instead of carrying a copy; the sweep
(scripts/reconcile.py) reads its stall windows from here; the documentation
(docs/lane-contract.md) is RENDERED from here; and the integration harness
asserts the live board against it on every trunk commit.
Every clause carries `enforced_from`: the wave phase at which the harness may
assert it. The harness asserts only clauses whose phase has shipped, and FAILS
when a clause's phase has passed with nothing implementing it. That is what
makes this a schedule that checks itself rather than a description.
JSON, not YAML: scripts/linear_ops.py imports the reader on every product
repo's agent job, where there is no pip install and PyYAML is not guaranteed.
Regenerate the document after any edit:
python3 scripts/lane_contract.py render
Check the live board against it:
python3 scripts/lane_contract.py check --live
Wave 1.5's phases, and how far the wave has actually shipped. `current` is
advanced by the operator prove-cards (DRE-2760..DRE-2768) — and advancing it
is the whole act: every clause at or below it must have an implementation or
the harness fails.

titles.0: the checks that must exist before anything moves
titles.1: Linear set up and the Intake lane visible
titles.2: the lane contract asserted by the harness
titles.3: the gates proven against every card type
titles.4: the agents changed before they touch a card
titles.5: cards flow through the new front door
titles.6: the old structure archived, and the wave closed

why: The transition a card makes leaving the planning segment, past which every
card carries a verdict. Layer 1 of the guard polices the lanes downstream
of it and nothing upstream, because upstream no verdict can exist yet.
Named after the transition, never after a description of the lanes on one
side of it: a description drifts and takes the guard's scope with it.

_readme: Retired board names, accepted on INPUT so a board mid-rename still resolves
to the right lane. An alias is not a lane and is never written out by the
contract; scripts/linear_ops.py inverts this map for the one write path that
still needs the old name. Delete an entry once no board carries it — this is
the ONE place the retired name survives, and both directions read it here.
Each entry carries the shim marker DRE-2722's sweep looks for, so the
exemption is a declared intent on the line itself and not a path allow-list.
The console's own state vocabulary, which must not diverge from the board.
It lives in another repository, so the harness locates the module by name in
that repo's tree and reads the named symbol. When it cannot reach it, the
clause reports UNEVALUATED — never a pass — and becomes a hard failure from
the phase named on the rule.
Every actor permitted to move a card, and where it lives. A lane names
writers by key; the harness checks the key resolves here and that a writer
with a path still exists in this checkout — a lane whose writer was deleted
is a lane nothing can legally move a card out of.
It is also the ACTOR GLOSSARY the act registry binds to (DRE-2825):
`pipeline_act.problems()` refuses an act whose `next_actor` is not a key
here, so that an act cannot hand work to somebody nothing knows about. An
entry may therefore name an actor no lane lists — `release-train.yml` is
one, added by DRE-3521 for the six release acts. Being in this glossary is
not permission to move a card: permission is a lane naming the key in its
own `writers` clause, which is what `ready_lane_writers.py` reads.

relay.what: the dispatch Lambda — creates a card's first lane from an inbound event
relay.note: lives in agent-bureau (cloud/relay); no path to check from here

operator.what: a human, working in Linear or running a script by hand

plan.yml.what: the planner — writes an epic's children and moves the epic for approval

agent-task.yml.what: the build run — takes a card from Todo and reports where it landed

agent-fix.yml.what: the fix run — REQUEST_CHANGES or a merge conflict

qa-review.yml.what: the adversarial critic — writes the verdict the gate reads

merge-gate.yml.what: the gate — merges on CI green plus a bound APPROVE

linear-sync.yml.what: the merge seam — closes the card off GitHub's merge event

reconcile.py.what: the ~15-minute sweep — promotion, staleness nudges, unsticking

linear_ops.py.what: the guarded write layer every other writer goes through

mid_epic.py.what: mid-epic discovery — files a sibling into an approved epic

dead_run.py.what: the dead-run cap — parks a card that keeps dying

groomer.py.what: the groomer — moves ONE approved batch out of Intake, in order

critic_score.py.what: the critic's audit — moves a card the critic could not classify, with the reason on it

backlog_cutover.py.what: the retroactive pass — moves the legacy Backlog into Intake, promoter-reach cards first and then newest-first, with no exemption list

hand_work_migration.py.what: the one-time move of a person's work out of Todo into Hand-work (DRE-5323) — run by hand, dry first; moves only cards marked hand-built or no-code, and names any epic or finished card it finds without writing to it

release-train.yml.what: the release train — runs a surface's release script and verifies the tag it cut; it moves no card, and is here as the actor the six release acts name (DRE-3521)

hygiene.py.what: the hygiene agent — the hourly pass that clears mechanical rows, each move under a 🧹 receipt naming the evidence it read

guard.what: the lane guard — returns a card whose occupancy is unjustified

console.what: the console — files the week's agent-failure report as ONE no-code card for the CEO to read (DRE-4271)

entrance.text: Every writer that creates work writes here first — the relay, the planner, a mid-epic discovery, a human. There is no other valid first lane.
entrance.pending: DRE-2680 points every writer at Intake

exit.text: A classification exists: one-off, epic, or roll-up. There are exactly THREE ways out. Two are an approval the CEO gives. For a card nobody filed under an epic the way out is the groomer — it proposes a batch, the CEO approves it in Green Light, and the approved batch drains to Planning (groomer.py drain) — the drain moves what the free planner slots take, and every other card of the batch is QUEUED (DRE-5435): it stays here under the `groom-queued` label, listed in the `groom-queued` record on the groomer's standing card, and the bureau-pipeline sweep moves it to Planning one card per free slot, oldest batch first. One approval moves the whole batch; a queued card is never proposed again, and waiting in the queue is never escalated. For a card whose PARENT EPIC is being planned the way out is adoption (DRE-4668, on the CEO's signed answer of 2026-09-23): the planning exit writes the child's routing verdict and moves it to Backlog, where it waits — the epic's own green light is the approval for the cards filed under it, and nothing builds until the CEO moves that epic to In Progress. A child the verdict sends back to Planning is not adopted and stays here. The third is the Urgent fast path (DRE-4150, on point 2 of the same signed answer of 2026-09-17): the sweep moves a card to Planning on its next pass when it is not an epic, is at Urgent and was RAISED to Urgent (or created at it) after the rule's ship moment in config/urgent-fast-path.json — read off the card's own Linear history, never its label — carries no signed exclusion from the CEO on the groomer's standing card, and has no parent epic or one that is In Progress. At most three a sweep across the whole fleet, oldest raised first, counted off the receipts already posted on the board so two repos sweeping in the same minute move three between them; the rest wait for the next sweep and the run log names them. INTAKE_HOLD does not stop it — the hold pauses the groomer's drain, and an Urgent card waiting behind a pause is the opposite of the rule. The card carries a receipt naming the rule, posted just before the move; the move is read back off the card's lane, and a card whose move did not land is tried again on a later sweep, at most three attempts in all, before it is left to the groomer. A card that reached Planning is never moved by this rule again. Urgency skips the queue, not Planning's classifier and critic. AGE IS NOT AN EXIT: no card is moved out of this lane for being old, this lane carries no stall window, and there is no window of any length in its place (DRE-4141, on the CEO's signed answer of 2026-09-17). The sweep reports how many cards are waiting and how old the oldest is, and moves none of them for their age.

writers.text: Anything that creates a card, and the retroactive pass that moves the legacy Backlog in. ONE of them also moves a card onward, and only with an approval behind it: plan.yml adopts a planned epic's own children into Backlog (DRE-4668). The groomer's drain — the other way out — writes Planning rather than this lane, so it is named as a writer there.

evidence.text: The card exists and carries no classification yet.

lanes.name: Planning
lanes.stale_why: what a Planning card owes is a classification, and producing one is a planner run — plan.yml's job alone is capped at 45 minutes, two planner passes and two critic rounds (DRE-2736, DRE-2721)

entrance.text: The card has been classified as needing a plan.

exit.text: The card leaves by the route its shape declares (DRE-2844): a one-off the check can route goes straight to the build queue, carrying the routing verdict its own card decided and owing no plan artifact and no green light — one whose card names no exit condition to route on takes the escalation exit below instead (DRE-3038). A one-off is READ BEFORE IT MOVES (DRE-3041): the same pre-approval critic an epic gets, one bounded call between the shape stamp and the move, asking whether this is one pull request of work an agent can build unattended with nothing in it that is a decision. A pass moves the card, and nothing else does, because nothing reads a one-off after this point. Each other answer goes to whoever can act on it (DRE-5376): a SEND_BACK — a defect in the card an agent can fix from the repository and the card alone — is answered by the planner, which revises the card in place while it stays in this lane and posts what it changed per finding, and the critic reads it again on a fresh planning run; a one-off sent back `MAX_ROUNDS` times leaves for Triage with every finding named, never for the CEO's queue. A QUESTION — a decision only the CEO can make, whether the critic or the revising planner asks it — and a critic that could not run take the escalation exit below. An epic leaves for the CEO on a plan artifact, and for an epic it is still no artifact, no exit; a roll-up leaves as child epics under itself, each sent to Planning to be planned on its own. A card carrying no shape is CLASSIFIED by the run before it routes (DRE-3029) — one bounded read of the card against the three shapes, stamped with who made the call and on which model — so nothing sits here owing a stamp a person has to write by hand. An epic leaves for the CEO in Green Light only once BOTH critics have passed it on its current planning attempt (DRE-5268): a send-back at either critic is answered by the planner and re-read by that critic while the epic stays in this lane, and a plan that exhausts EITHER critic's round bound, or whose second critic produces no result twice, leaves for Triage with `needs-human` and the finding still open — never for the CEO's queue. There is a fourth exit and it is the only one that is not a plan: the run ESCALATES, with a reason stated in business terms, and the card parks in Green Light (DRE-2848) — the classifier takes it for a card it cannot place, and the planner for an epic whose reasoning is itself the deliverable. Hand-planning is that escalation and nothing else — no label, flag or lane skips this lane, and the one sanctioned bypass past the Todo gate, `break-glass`, returns the card here for the classification it went round. The SWEEP's stall exit (DRE-4124) parks a card nothing has happened to in the lane's stall window in Triage, with its reason on it and no label: a card no planner and no critic has read is the operator's to move and not the CEO's (DRE-5268), and a card nobody can move belongs in the queue of the person who can, rather than labeled `needs-human` and left sitting here — which is what froze thirteen cards, the oldest for thirty-five days. A card waiting in the planner line is not stalled (DRE-5177): under the fleet-wide planner cap it is served in line order, and the sweep escalates it to Triage only when its wait passes the bound in `config/planner-queue.json`.
exit.pending: DRE-2720 writes the epic's artifact, DRE-2844 branches the exit on the shape and DRE-2848 adds the escalation exit; the gate that refuses an epic's exit without an artifact is Phase 5

writers.text: The planner, the sweep that re-triggers it, a build run handing back a card that turned out to be an epic, a build run whose turn-cap death stopped before implementation green and is sent back to be cut smaller (the `replan` write, DRE-4366), the groomer draining a batch the CEO approved, the sweep's Urgent fast path moving a card raised to Urgent after that rule shipped (DRE-4150), the critic's audit moving a card it could not classify, the guarded write layer every automated card-minting seam goes through — the Todo gate returning a card it cannot repair, the one-off producer, and the medic/watch seams that file a fresh card (DRE-2858) — and a human. And the hygiene agent, returning from Green Light a row that was never a decision — a planner that died, a classifier transport failure, a child without acceptance criteria, an escalation that asks for a split or an access, a stall park — with the cause named (DRE-5365).

evidence.text: The plan artifact on the card: business case, KPIs as data, risk, outcome.

entrance.text: Five kinds of row, and no other (DRE-5268, DRE-4271). (a) A plan arrives only after BOTH critics passed it on its current planning attempt — the evidence is a `plan-critic: stage=post … result=PASS` record on the epic. (b) The planner escalated a business question, in plain English with a recommendation, and stated why (DRE-2848): every escalation the plan route makes, the classifier's for a card it cannot place and the planner's for an epic whose reasoning is itself the deliverable, each stated in business terms or refused. On the one-off route that is the critic's QUESTION, or the revising planner's own, and a critic that decided nothing — never a card the critic sent back for a defect, which the planner revises, and never the one-off round bound, which parks in Triage (DRE-5376). (c) The fleet was at its cap of epics in motion when the CEO approved an epic, so the planner labeled it `epic-queued`, recorded the approval on the epic in the ⏸️ receipt of that same name stating the epic's place in line, and returned it here to wait in line for the sweep (DRE-5129) — proposed by the operator and accepted by the CEO's approval of DRE-5268; the row asks nothing of the CEO, it shows where his approved work is in the line. (d) A build in flight stopped on something only a person can settle: the build run's escalate-by-exception question (DRE-1655: ambiguous intent, a risky change, or a business A-vs-B decision the CEO should own, posted as a plain-English question), or the merge gate is holding a green, approved pull request for a required code-owner review and moved the card here to ask the person the repository's rules name (DRE-4341 — only when the calling repo's merge-gate stub wakes the gate on a submitted review, because the sweep dispatches nothing for a card in this lane). Kind (d) predates DRE-5268 and carries no recommendation — the agent stopped precisely where it could not choose, and a review request has nothing to recommend — so it is its own kind and never read as (b). (e) The console filed the week's agent-failure report as one `no-code` card for the CEO to read (DRE-4271) — proposed by the CEO's own decision of 2026-09-18 and accepted by his approval of DRE-4271; the row asks nothing of him but to read it and close it. It is neither a question nor a plan nor a defect, so no sweep or keeper moves it, re-sends it to Planning or closes it, its lack of acceptance criteria is not a thing to fix, and only the CEO closes it. A row of this kind is recognized by its title `What broke the agents — week ending <Saturday> (PT)`, its `no-code` label and its description's first line, which opens `Weekly agent report — Green Light kind weekly-report`. Its write site lives in agent-bureau (`console/backend/weekly_agent_report_card.py`, DRE-5020), outside this repository, so it has no `arrivals` record. `arrivals` names every way a row is written into this lane from this repository, one record per site; `callers` on a record whose site is a Python function names the units permitted to reach it, because a write made through a function is attributed to its caller.

exit.text: The CEO answers: an approved plan activates and its children promote through the dependency gate, with no review after the approval — both critics read it before it arrived here (DRE-5268) — an answered escalation returns to Todo, a rejected one goes to Backlog. A queued epic is started by the sweep when the count of epics in motion falls under the cap, the highest Linear Priority first and the oldest approval on a tie, by moving it to In Progress, which fires the same activate route the CEO's own approval does; an epic already in motion that is re-approved after a mid-epic amendment starts past the cap rather than waiting; and an epic that leaves this lane any other way (re-planned after an amendment, handed back to Planning for a review it missed, parked, canceled) has left the line and loses the `epic-queued` label, so a re-planned epic arriving here again waits for a fresh approval (DRE-5129). Or the hygiene agent sends a row back to Planning that was never a decision, with the cause named; it never approves, and a real question stays here (DRE-5365).

exit.text: The verdict's destination is reached, and the sweep is what reaches it (DRE-3385). Which verdict lands where is config/routing-verdicts.json's to say, and the sweep reads that file, never this sentence. It promotes a FLEET card to Todo once the dependency gate clears, the WIP cap has room and — for a child of an epic — both critics passed the plan on its current planning attempt before the green light (DRE-3059, DRE-5268). The sweep promotes a WORKBENCH or OPERATOR card to its verdict's destination on the same gates too, stamping the marks its verdict declares — `hand-built`, plus `no-code` for OPERATOR — before the move, so the card never sits there unmarked; nothing is dispatched for it, it takes no slot under the WIP cap, and the receipt says whose turn it is. Under DRE-5240 that destination is Hand-work, the lane where a person's work waits, and FLEET alone goes to Todo (DRE-5321, DRE-5322). A PARKED card does not leave, and is never reported as stalled; a NEEDS WORK card goes back to Planning, which is the planner's move and not the sweep's. A card carrying no verdict at all is not promoted, whether or not it has a parent epic: the epic's approval says the PLAN was approved, never who builds this piece of it. A verdict approves ONE trip through Planning (DRE-4962): a card that has entered Intake, Green Light, Triage, Canceled, Duplicate or Done since its newest verdict is not promoted — the sweep refuses it `stale-verdict`, says once on the card when the verdict was written, which of those lanes it passed through since and that it needs Planning again to be built, and leaves it here. A later exit from Planning, or for a child its epic's green light, is a fresh approval, because the planning exit does not re-stamp a verdict the card already carries. The check reads the card's lane history, so it is the last gate, asked only of a card every other gate has passed; a history Linear cannot return holds the card that sweep and says nothing on it.
exit.pending: the sweep carries every verdict it promotes out of this lane and refuses the rest (DRE-2724, DRE-3385); asserting the transitions needs the history Phase 5 records; DRE-5240 pointed WORKBENCH and OPERATOR at Hand-work (DRE-5321) and the sweep carries them there (DRE-5322)

writers.text: The planner and mid-epic discovery create here; the sweep and the dead-run cap park here; and the build run parks the card it could not build — a stated blocker, or a run that kept dying past the cap (DRE-2859). A person also lands a card here by sending it back from Green Light — the rejected answer that lane's exit names — or by moving it here by hand; that move approves nothing, and the `stale-verdict` refusal above is what keeps the sweep from building it (DRE-4962). And the hygiene agent, returning a Triage card whose mechanical defect it fixed — a prose blocker made true by the relation it added, a dependency loop a Done card already broke, a retired-repo card marked hand-built and parked — never to Todo (DRE-5365).

writers.text: ONE promoter, and it is the sweep: reconcile.py's promote_ready() is the only thing that moves an epic's child into this lane, whether the 15-minute cron reaches it or plan.yml's activate route runs it the moment the second critic passes — the route triggers that promoter, it never promotes itself. It releases a child only once the epic carries a `plan-critic: stage=post result=PASS` marker for the current planning attempt (DRE-3059). It moves a FLEET card here, unmarked: FLEET declares no marks. A WORKBENCH or OPERATOR card is not promoted here — the same promoter carries it to Hand-work, its marks stamped before that move (DRE-3385, DRE-5322). The build run takes cards out of it.

lanes.name: In Review
lanes.stale_why: the folded lane keeps the longer of the two windows the pair had (120 and 60) — a shorter one re-dispatches reviews that are simply still running
lanes.note: Folded from the two review lanes DRE-2726 retired (DRE-2818 deleted their entries once Linear archived the states). Both meant 'a pull request is open and being checked'; the sweep now keys off the evidence — a verdict bound to the head — rather than off which of two lanes the card sat in.

entrance.text: A pull request is open on the card's branch and is being checked: by the critic, by the verifier, or by the merge gate. The card may arrive here from ANY pre-review lane — Intake, Triage, Planning, Backlog, Todo or In Progress — and not only from In Progress: a pull request opened outside the relay's dispatch has no agent-task run behind it to have written In Progress, so qa-review.yml advances the card itself when the pull request opens (DRE-4179). Green Light is not a pre-review lane for this route: it is the CEO's own queue and a branch existing does not take a card out of it. The one move out of Green Light into this lane is the merge gate's release (DRE-4341): once the required code-owner review it was holding for has landed, it moves the card back here before it merges — only a card it parked itself, recognized by its own hold marker, never a card someone else put in Green Light.

exit.text: GitHub merges the pull request and linear-sync writes Done — or the pull request is gone and the card is requeued under the dead-run cap. Or the hygiene agent closes a proof card whose merged record meets every criterion in its table, under the CEO's standing rule (DRE-5365).

writers.text: The build run puts cards here; the critic, the gate, the fix run and the sweep move them on. The sweep also FILES a card straight into this lane for every dependabot pull request (DRE-3665): the pull request already exists and is already being checked, so there is nothing to plan or dispatch. And the hygiene agent, moving a proof card from Triage to the lane its already-open pull request says it is in (DRE-5365).

evidence.text: An open pull request; and, once the critic has run, a verdict bound to the head sha.

entrance.text: GitHub merged the card's pull request. The merge event, never an agent's claim. Or the hygiene agent closes, on the merge event it read back off GitHub and never on its own claim, a card the merge seam did not close: a build card whose pull request merged while the seam was not watching, or a proof card whose merged record meets every criterion in its own table, under the CEO's standing rule of 2026-09-30 that a proof shown proven with evidence is approved (DRE-5365).
entrance.pending: needs the transition history Phase 5 records

exit.text: None. Done is terminal, and the guarded write layer refuses to un-complete a card that reached it.

writers.text: The merge seam, the sweep's merged-PR backstop, and a human closing an operator card. And the hygiene agent, for exactly those two classes, each under a 🧹 receipt naming the pull request and its merge time.

evidence.text: The merge commit on the card's own branch.

lanes.name: Triage
lanes.off_flow_reason: the guard's own destination for a card returned three times — policing it would bounce the sink straight back to Intake and loop

entrance.text: The card itself is malformed and cannot proceed as written: an unroutable repo label, an archived repo, a card the readiness guard has returned three times. Also a plan that exhausted either critic's round bound before Green Light, or whose second critic produced no result twice, parked with `needs-human` and the finding still open (DRE-5268); a one-off card the pre-approval critic sent back `MAX_ROUNDS` times, or whose revision the planner did not finish, parked with every finding named — a revision loop that does not converge is a defect, not a decision (DRE-5376); and a card that sat in Planning past that lane's window with nothing happening to it — the sweep's stall exit parks it in Triage with the reason on it and no label (DRE-4124 as amended by DRE-5268). And one card for a stalled groom queue (DRE-5435): approved cards queued in Intake for a planner slot, a slot free, nothing released and nothing changing the queue for the planner line's own bound — the bureau-pipeline sweep CREATES that card in Triage, `no-code` and with no `agent:*` role, the whole notice in its body, and never a second while it is open. The queue is the pipeline's to unstick, not the CEO's to decide, so it is never sent to Green Light.
entrance.pending: DRE-2723 defines what may be parked here

exit.text: Somebody fixes the card, and it re-enters at Intake. Triage is not a decision queue — a card waiting on the CEO belongs in Green Light. An operator re-enters a parked epic by clearing `needs-human` and moving it to Planning: a plan run fires for any card entering Planning, the route opens a fresh planning attempt, and the planner and both critics read the plan again (DRE-5268). The plan run that fires when an `agent:planner` card ENTERS Triage is refused by the plan-gate when the card carries `needs-human` or its newest comment is a `planning-stall-park` note, so a park stays parked until a person moves it (DRE-5277). Or the hygiene agent fixes the mechanical defect and returns the card to Backlog, never Todo (DRE-5365).

writers.text: Whatever found the defect: the relay, the sweep, either agent run, the planner parking a plan at either critic's bound (DRE-5268) or a one-off card at the one-off critic's bound (DRE-5376), or a human.

evidence.text: The defect, named on the card by whatever bounced it.

lanes.name: Canceled
lanes.off_flow_reason: terminal and off the path; the card makes no claim to justify

entrance.text: A human decided the work will not be done — or, for a dependabot card, the pull request it was filed for closed unmerged (DRE-3665) — or, for a card the CEO agreed to cancel on a groomer proposal, the groomer's drain moved it with his reason written onto the card (DRE-4677). In all three a human decided; what differs is who wrote it down. Or, fourth, the card is a returned child of an epic that the planner split into sibling cards under the same epic, and it was canceled with those siblings named on it (DRE-5242): nothing is dropped, because every piece of the work is a sibling, and the original is canceled rather than Done because no code shipped. Or, fifth, the card's parent epic is itself Canceled or Duplicate and the hygiene agent canceled the child with the parent's state named on it (DRE-5365): the human decided on the parent, and the agent wrote the consequence down for a child that has no children of its own.
entrance.pending: needs the transition history Phase 5 records

exit.pending: needs the transition history Phase 5 records

writers.text: A human — and two mechanisms, each for exactly one class, neither of them deciding anything. The sweep, for a card it filed for a dependabot pull request that then closed without merging (DRE-3665): dependabot superseding its own pull request, or a person closing it, is the decision; the sweep records it. The groomer's drain, for a card the CEO agreed to cancel on a groomer proposal (DRE-4677): the groomer proposes cancellations and the CEO agrees card by card in the console, and his per-card agree is the decision — the drain writes Canceled for exactly the cards on the approved proposal's Cancel table that he did not exclude, with the reason he read written onto each one as a comment. The principle the clause states is unchanged in both: a human decided. What changes is who writes it down. And the planner (plan.yml), for a returned child of an epic (DRE-5242): a card that came back to Planning, was read afresh as an epic, and is itself a child of an epic is split into sibling cards under that epic, and the planner run that filed them cancels the original with a comment naming every sibling — never Done, because no code shipped (standards/card-quality.md, How to split). That one is the pipeline's own act, narrowed to that one class, and it drops no work: every piece of the card lives on in a sibling carrying its own routing verdict. And the hygiene agent, for that one class only, a childless card under a Canceled or Duplicate parent, never deciding anything.

evidence.text: A human's decision, on the card.
